note: Unit prices only, extracted from the vendors' own pricing pages. Every number carries the page it came from and the date it was read. This file is the data layer: the CLI, the MCP server and any page are renderers of it.
disclosure: Links marked affiliate are a9n9's affiliate links: a9n9 earns a commission if you buy through them. Prices are the vendors' own and are not affected.

firecrawl.name: Firecrawl
firecrawl.affiliate_disclosure: affiliate link: a9n9 earns a commission if you buy through it
firecrawl.buyer_offer: New users get 10% off their first purchase through the affiliate link (stated on partners.dub.co/firecrawl).
firecrawl.credit_rule: 1 credit = 1 page scraped or 1 crawl page. JSON format and prompt-injection checks add 4 credits per page.
traps: The '$16/month' figure is the annual-billed rate ($190/year), not the monthly price of $19.
Searches and pages share one credit balance; a search is 2 credits, so '5,000 credits' is 2,500 searches on Hobby.

elevenlabs.name: ElevenLabs
elevenlabs.affiliate_disclosure: affiliate link: a9n9 earns a commission if you buy through it

startup_grant.value_claim_text: That's over 680 hours of Agents usage. More than $5,500+ in value.
startup_grant.eligibility_note: The page addresses early-stage startups that are building voice into a product. Access is by application at grants-application, not a coupon code, and the program's terms can change.

free_tier.note: The plan column prints 'Characters included' and its own minute column beside each model: 10,000 ~10 min on v4 at $0.08/1,000, 20,000 ~20 min on v4 Turbo at $0.04/1,000. The Creative plans page states the same free allowance as 10k credits; on the API column the unit is characters.

credit_costs.pool_note: All products draw from one shared monthly credit pool, so the same credits can be spent on any of them and using one leaves fewer for the others.
credit_costs.char_rule: For V2 Multilingual models, 1 text character equals 1 credit. For V2 Flash/Turbo English and V2.5 Flash/Turbo Multilingual models, discounted pricing applies for API usage, costing between 0.5 and 1 credit per character.
credit_costs.rollover: Your credit allowance resets at the start of each billing cycle. Unused credits roll over for up to two months — up to 2x your monthly quota — so a balance can reach at most 3x the monthly quota, as long as the paid subscription stays active and is not downgraded or cancelled. Rollover does not apply to the Free plan, and downgrading or cancelling forfeits unused credits.
credit_costs.free_tier_disabled_note: ElevenLabs' own Help Center lists the message "Unusual activity detected. Free Tier usage disabled. If you are using proxy/VPN you might need to purchase a paid plan to not trigger our abuse detectors" — so the free tier can be switched off by the vendor's abuse detector, and its stated cause is proxy or VPN use.

traps: Two of the vendor's own pages print two different allowances for the same $22 Creator plan: /pricing/api lists 275,000 characters, while /pricing lists 121,000 credits. Its FAQ says 1 text character equals 1 credit for V2 Multilingual models, which would make those the same quantity at $0.1818 per 1,000 characters — 2.27x the API page's $0.080 — yet the API page's own FAQ says API usage is billed in US dollars, not credits. Re-read 2026-11-09T01:3xZ: the two pages are not reconcilable from their own text, so both numbers are quoted as dated and neither is converted into the other. Settle it before repeating either rate as 'the' ElevenLabs price.
The API ladder is flat: $990/12.375M = $0.080/1k, i.e. no volume discount. Buying a bigger plan does not lower the unit price.
First-month promos (Starter $1, Creator $11, advertised as ending 2026-11-16) are not prices; list price is $6/$22.
elevenlabs.ladder_note: Characters included per month on the v4 column of /pricing/api, list prices. The page's own minute column divides characters by 1,000 ("75,000 ~75 min"), so the vendor's own conversion is 1,000 chars per spoken minute, not 900.
elevenlabs.promo_note: First-month promos are printed on the same page and change: 2026-11-08 showed Starter first month $1 and Creator first month $11 against list prices $6/$22. Promos are not prices.

deepgram.name: Deepgram
deepgram.unit: three units: per minute (STT), per minute (Voice Agent), per 1,000 characters (TTS)
deepgram.affiliate_disclosure: affiliate link: a9n9 earns a commission if you buy through it
traps: The $0.075 per minute headline on this page is the Voice Agent (STT + managed LLM + TTS), NOT speech-to-text. Speech-to-text alone is $0.0043-$0.0092 per minute by model and tier, i.e. 8-17x cheaper than the number usually quoted. Reading the agent rate as an STT rate makes Deepgram look ~17x more expensive than it is.
Deepgram's $200 credit is the free tier; it expires, so it is not a price.
Aura-2 is $0.030/1k characters pay-as-you-go and $0.027 on Growth; Aura-1 is $0.015/$0.0135. The TTS side does have a tier ladder even though the STT headline does not.

computed_facts.el_agent_vs_dg_agent: All-in agent minutes: ElevenLabs Agents $0.080 vs Deepgram Voice Agent Standard $0.075 pay-as-you-go ($0.068 Growth). ElevenLabs is 6.7% more on PAYG and 17.6% more against Growth, and on ElevenLabs' two Realtime tiers the LLM is billed separately.
computed_facts.el_tts_vs_dg_tts: Per character: ElevenLabs v4 $0.080/1k vs Deepgram Aura-2 $0.030/1k (2.7x) and Aura-1 $0.015/1k (5.3x). At 900 chars per spoken minute that is $0.072 vs $0.027 vs $0.0135 per minute of synthesized speech.
computed_facts.dg_stt_vs_dg_agent: Deepgram's own STT ($0.0043-$0.0092/min) is 8-17x cheaper per minute than its Voice Agent ($0.075/min), because the agent minute bundles a managed LLM and TTS.
computed_facts.chars_per_minute_range: Characters per spoken minute swings 600-1,000 depending on speaker and pacing: a 67% swing in any per-character estimate.
